newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen rising.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee ended 0.10 up in the kerb market at 42.35 to the dollar on Sunday in low demand due to a liquidity crunch, dealers said.
Dealer Salman Iqbal of ARY International Exchange said the rupee was likely to post fresh gains on low demand owing to a shortage of funds and heavy dollar supplies from the Gulf.
The State (central) bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on October 22, was 40.1200/40.3206 to the dollar.
The premium on the foreign exchange bearer certificates closed unchanged at 6.20 percent. -- Ibrahim Khan 9221-5685192
